articles.author: Working Mass: The Massachusetts DSA Labor Outlet
articles.content_excerpt: Madrid in Winter 2026, six months before the eviction of Maricarmen (Working Mass) By : Javier Moreno Zacarés This was originally published in New Left Review on October 9, 2026. Fifteen years after the indignados occupied the Puerta del Sol, Madrid’s central plaza is once again the locus of a mass movement that has brought Spain to a political impasse. How are we back here again? The immediate trigger was the eviction of an elderly tenant. Maricarmen Abascal, who had occupied her rent-capped apartment in central Madrid since 1956, was expelled from her home on 23 September after the investment fund Urbagestión acquired the property and exploited a legal loophole to quintuple her rent. articles.title: No to abolition
articles.author: Socialist Forum
articles.content_excerpt: Editorial note: The following is a letter response to Hazel W.’s piece, “ In Defense of Abolition .” In July, the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) amended its program to call for “abolishing the police and prison system.” Taken literally, that is a mistake. Society needs institutions to patrol and isolate the dangerous few. Even the most radical socialist societies understood this. For example, the Paris Commune — that libertarian-left experiment — had a prefecture of police. It established neighborhood watches and incarcerated thousands as “hostages of the people of Paris.” The commune is not proof of concept for prison and police abolition. articles.title: Major Jason Watson
articles.author: Jeffrey Sterling
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. For almost two months, an Air Force officer has been sitting alone in a cell, twenty-four hours a day. When they let him out to eat or exercise, he’s still alone, according to his attorney . His name is Major Jason Watson. He hasn’t been convicted of anything. Under military law he is presumed innocent, yet he’s still in that cell. I know something about solitary confinement. I also know what it feels like when a government would rather silence you than answer for its transgressions. That’s why I can’t stay quiet about Major Watson. articles.title: UFCW Members Protect Local Election After Sham Merger Attempt
articles.author: Lisa Xu
articles.content_excerpt: An insurgent slate is challenging the longtime incumbents in Local 8-Golden State, one of the largest locals in the United Food and Commercial Workers (UFCW), in what may be the local’s first competitive election in decades. And now, after protecting the election from a sham merger attempt that would have canceled the election, the battle is on. Ballots are set to be mailed on November 21. But when members first saw the election notice in the local’s newsletter, they discovered a big “but.” The notice stated that the election would not proceed if Local 8 merged with another union, the Staffing Agencies Federated Employees (SAFE), before the end of the year. articles.title: Alberta’s Separation Ballot Ended With a Whimper
articles.author: Gerard Di Trolio
articles.content_excerpt: No country treats referendums as less definitive than Canada. Two sovereignty referendums in Quebec have not totally put to bed the independence question in la belle province , and in spite of declining referendum support, the new Parti Québécois government is promising a third when Donald Trump leaves office. Voters rejected a set of constitutional amendments known as the Charlottetown Accord in 1992, but constitutional issues continue to fester with no federal government willing to touch them. This history matters when considering Alberta’s recent referendum. articles.content_excerpt: Following a stunning, inspiring turnaround driven by mass mobilization of the Brazilian people, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won his fourth presidential election. articles.author: Gilbert Achcar
articles.content_excerpt: To fully grasp what has been going on since October 7, 2023, in the territories newly reoccupied by Israel in Gaza and Lebanon, it is necessary to examine the pattern of these occupations against previous ones conducted by the Zionist state. As is well known, the very birth of Israel was inseparable from occupation. The new state proclaimed on May 15, 1948, spanned over 56 percent of British Mandate Palestine between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea — the territory attributed to the “Jewish State” by the partition resolution adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in November 1947. articles.title: 1956 Was a Missed Opportunity for Socialist Reform in Poland
articles.author: Gavin Rae
articles.content_excerpt: In June 1956, a delegation of renowned British left-wing economists, including Joan Robinson and Maurice Dobb, traveled to Poland to learn about its socialist transformation. The newly installed socialist government had driven through a program of economic modernization, as the country industrialized and urbanized, and free universal health care and education were being provided for the first time. While visiting the city of Poznań, they expected to admire the material achievements of the new Polish People’s Republic (PRL). Instead they witnessed Polish soldiers manning Soviet tanks as they put down a workers’ revolt.
